tip: sua agrees with the thing owned, not the owner, so la sua ragazza can mean his or her girlfriend.
dare fastidio means to bother, built like piacere: mi dà fastidio il rumore is the noise gives annoyance to me.
suonare is to play an instrument; giocare is only for games and sports: suona il violino.
The indefinite article is uno, not un, before s plus consonant or z: uno studente, uno zaino.
mi dispiace means I am sorry, literally it displeases me; it works backwards like piacere.
For plural liked things, piacere becomes piacciono: ti piacciono i miei quadri = the paintings please you.
non plus più means no more or no longer: non ci sono più biglietti is there are no more tickets.
Volere che takes the subjunctive; in the past that is the imperfect subjunctive: volevo che tu sapessi.

english: The water is fresh and good.
tip: fresca means cool or fresh, not cold; cold would be fredda: l'acqua è fresca.

target: Ci sono due camere da letto.
tip: C'è is 'there is', ci sono is 'there are': ci sono due camere = there are two rooms. Ci here just means 'there'.

target: Ci sono tanti ristoranti in centro.
tip: Quantity words agree with their noun: ristoranti is masculine plural, so 'many' becomes tanti, giving tanti ristoranti.

target: Gli basta poco per essere felice.
english: He doesn't need much to be happy.
tip: bastare works like piacere: gli basta poco means little is enough for him.

target: La stazione è vicina a casa.
english: The station is close to home.
tip: vicino needs a before what it is near: vicina a casa means close to home.

english: Before he left, I said goodbye to him.
tip: prima che forces the subjunctive: prima che partisse means before he left.

english: I wish I were on vacation right now!
tip: magari plus the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish: magari fossi means I wish I were.
di shows what something is made of: di lana means made of wool.

english: The sugar is in the jar.
tip: Masculine nouns starting with z take lo, not il: lo zucchero, lo zaino.

english: The hotel is clean and welcoming.
tip: The h in hotel is silent, so it counts as vowel-initial and takes l': you write l'hotel, not il hotel.

target: La pagella arriva a fine anno.
english: The report card comes at the end of the year.
tip: Fixed time phrases like a fine anno drop the article: a fine anno, not alla fine dell'anno.

target: Il calcio è popolare in Italia.
tip: Countries take in with no article: in Italia means in Italy, in Francia is in France.

target: Mi piace fare colazione al bar.
english: I like having breakfast at the cafe.
tip: Before an infinitive, piacere stays singular: mi piace fare colazione = I like having breakfast. The activity is the subject.

target: Il treno è più veloce dell'autobus.
english: The train is faster than the bus.
tip: Comparisons use più plus di for than: più veloce dell'autobus means faster than the bus.
Nationalities ending in -ese use one form for both genders; the plural is -esi: olandesi.
The adjective matches the noun in number: a masculine plural noun takes -i, so documentari sono educativi.
giocare takes a before a sport or game: giocano a calcio means they play soccer.
incidente is a false friend: gli incidenti means accidents, not incidents.

english: The men work in a factory.
tip: uomo has an irregular plural, uomini, which takes the article gli.

target: Gli asparagi alla griglia sono deliziosi con olio d'oliva.
english: Grilled asparagus are delicious with olive oil.
tip: Alla plus a noun names a cooking style: alla griglia = grilled, alla romana = Roman-style.
Italian has cold rather than is cold: ha freddo = she is cold. Saying sono freddo would make you a cold object.
Weather uses fare, not essere: fa freddo = it's cold, fa caldo = it's hot.
